# Core Rules

Read for every task: the `must` rules of the principles (except repo setup, see `repo-setup.md`) and a few cross-cutting rules.

- PRIN-14 must: Write no comment where the code already says it, except API docs of exported or public functions (GO-18, PY-13).
  Good: `dns.Create(ctx, opts)` with no comment.
  Bad: `// create the dns entries` above that call.
- PRIN-15 must: Comment only to give a reason, unit, assumption or non-obvious constraint, and put it above the line or constant.
  Good: `STREAM_READ_TIMEOUT = 90  # seconds, three missed pulses`
  Bad: `# set the timeout to 90`
- PRIN-19 must: Keep a file header to at most 3 lines; put longer design notes in docs.
  Good: `# Which modules do something is decided by dev.* options.`
  Bad: a 20-line header repeating the module list.
- PRIN-01 must: Write the shortest text that is still complete.
  Good: `Deploy the stack with pulumi up.`
  Bad: `In order to deploy the stack, you will now want to run the following command.`
- PRIN-02 must: Leave out filler and do not write around a point; say it directly.
  Good: `The cache is cleared on restart.`
  Bad: `It is worth noting that the cache will generally be cleared whenever a restart occurs.`
- PRIN-04 must: Be precise: give exact values, units, versions, identifiers and paths instead of vague words.
  Good: `timeout: 90 s, three missed pulses`.
  Bad: `a short timeout`.
- PRIN-05 must: Do not include text that adds no information: restating a heading, the code, the diff or the previous sentence; API docs of exported or public functions are excepted (GO-18, PY-13).
  Good: a command block without a paragraph that repeats the command in words.
  Bad: `This section describes the installation.` under `## Installation`.
- PRIN-32 must: Write log messages lowercase without a trailing period, in every language; free-text error messages follow the same form, while error codes, machine-readable identifiers, acronyms and code-like tokens keep their original case, also at the start.
  Good: `failed to create the client: %w`; `error creating project: <name>` (failing operation, then the offending value); the code `ONYX_ACTION_ERROR` stays uppercase.
  Bad: `Error!`; `Failed to create the client.`
- PRIN-33 must: Remove debug prints before committing.
  Good: the commit contains only the fix; the `print(resp)` used while debugging is gone.
  Bad: `print("here", resp)` left in the client code.
- PRIN-26 must: Never commit a secret in clear; deliver secrets through a secret store, an external secret object or an out-of-band file. [tool:gitleaks]
  Good: `kind: ExternalSecret` that references `remoteRef.key: app/db-password`.
  Bad: `password: hunter2` in a values file.
- PRIN-08 must: Keep the tone grounded; no exaggeration, hype or superlatives; a plain factual statement or feature list is not hype.
  Good: `This should fix the timeout.`
  Bad: `This completely eliminates all timeout problems!`
- PRIN-09 must: Write in English by default, for code, comments, docs, commits and issues.
  Good: `// retry once if the socket is closed` and a commit `fix: handle empty response`.
  Bad: a German comment or commit subject in a public repo.
- PRIN-10 must: Write impersonal, present-tense, declarative prose; address the reader as "you" only in direct instructions; no marketing wording (superlatives and hype adjectives such as "powerful", "seamless"); a factual feature list is fine.
  Good: `The stack is deployed via pulumi up.`
  Bad: `You will love how seamlessly the powerful stack deploys.`
- PRIN-11 must: Do not use em dashes; use a colon, comma, semicolon or parentheses; use `->` only in commands.
  Good: `v6-only features are unavailable; their calls fail.`
  Bad: the same sentence with an em dash between the clauses.
- PRIN-12 must: Do not use emoji in code, comments, docs, headings, commit subjects, PR titles, replies or script output; generated content such as an all-contributors table is exempt.
  Good: `done: 3 created, 1 skipped`.
  Bad: a check-mark symbol prefix on status lines.
- PRIN-13 must: Do not decorate: no banners, box-drawing lines, ASCII art frames or all-caps emphasis in output, comments or docs.
  Good: `### docker ###` as a plain section label in provisioning scripts.
  Bad: a framed multi-line header made of drawing characters.
- PRIN-40 must: Pin every dependency, image, chart, action and tool to an exact version; never `latest`, except runner labels such as `ubuntu-latest`. Pin by digest only for an unstable tag.
  Good: `image: nginx:1.27.2` and `uses: actions/checkout@<full sha> # v4.2.2`.
  Bad: `image: nginx:latest`.
- PRIN-42 must: Lint every file type in the repo (code, Markdown, shell, YAML); the gates pass before work is done.
  Good: the gates `ruff check`, `markdownlint`, `shellcheck` and `yamllint` all pass before the change is called done.
  Bad: ruff passes while the new `deploy.sh` and `README.md` were never linted.
- PRIN-44 must: Suppress a finding only with a narrow, named suppression and a written reason; remove it when the cause is gone. [tool:golangci-lint]
  Good: `//nolint:mnd // 0o600 is the correct permission for private keys`
  Bad: `//nolint`
- PRIN-50 must: Pin the linters in `mise.toml` so one `mise install` provides them.
  Good: `shellcheck = "0.11.0"` in `[tools]` of `mise.toml`.
  Bad: shellcheck installed by hand or through the system package manager.
- COMMIT-17 must: Add no attribution to commits or PR text: no `Co-Authored-By` trailer for agents and no "Generated with" line. Add no `Signed-off-by` either (PR-18 covers PR text).
  Good: `fix: handle empty response` and nothing after the subject.
  Bad: a trailing `Co-Authored-By:` line naming an agent, or `Signed-off-by:`.
- PR-18 must: Add no attribution to PR text: no "Generated with" line and no AI trailer, whatever the tool's default adds (COMMIT-17).
  Good: body `fix #12` and nothing after it.
  Bad: a body ending in a "Generated with ..." line or a `Co-Authored-By:` AI trailer.
- DOC-06 must: Write Markdown prose as one paragraph per line, without hard wraps; code comments follow the formatter's line length.
  Good: one paragraph on one line, however long it runs.
  Bad: the same paragraph broken at 80 columns.
- DOC-11 prefer: Use American spelling.
- PRIN-16 prefer: Start inline comments lowercase and end them without a period; Go doc comments are the exception (GO-17).

Avoid (AI-Era Artifacts):

- Long documents and READMEs that grow with every change.
- Banners, box-drawing characters, emoji, status symbols.
- Em dashes.
- `Args:` and `Returns:` docblocks.
- Long file headers and doc comments on every private method.
- Restating the diff in a commit or PR body.
